Since the upvoat limit was increased to 100, there are now complaints that it's too high and low effort posts are getting upvoats when they don't deserve it thus making their way to the front page.

First suggestion:

Reduce the upvoat limit back down to 10 or 20, but do this per sub. So, every subverse to which a user is subscribed will allow them X upvoats per day. This would prompt people to be more conservative and be more likely to encourage quality content.

Second Suggestion: (I personally don't think this is all that good of a choice, but I like options)

Change the voat limit to be a function of CCP in that every new user starts with a base amount (i.e. 10 per day) and then it increases as a percentage in relation to your total CCP. For example, if we use 10%, then at 100 CCP you would get 20 voats daily (10 + 10), at 200 CCP you'd get 30 voats (10 + 20) and so on and so forth. After a certain threshold it can either increase exponentially, or be removed altogether. This encourages people to contribute to the community and further recognizes those that have contributed in a positive manner by allowing them a greater ability to shape the community in positive ways. As with any system, I recognize this has flaws and drawbacks, and can absolutely be abused.

Downvoats:

In either case, I believe downvoats should also have a daily limit (if they don't already). This would be good in order to prevent bridgading. It could/should also follow one of the above mentioned scenarios, though they don't necessarily need to be the same (i.e. upvoats can follow suggestion 1 but downvoats work as a function of CCP).

Depends how well you wish to hide the video. For example, if you wish to hide it really well you could:

  1. Add a nonsense title for the video i.e. "My kids birthday party"

  2. Flip the video, add 20% thick white edge border shadow and slightly desaturate the colors as to make it harder for any auto-detection to pick it up.

  3. Add subtle randomized level of grain to the audio output to make it harder for any auto-detection to pick it up

This is why we see so many movies with white patches, speed changed, sound randomly dropping. The auto detections look at the video frame by frame, taking the audio data and image data for a frame, and seeing if it matches within a slight margin of error against any movies in their database.

The goal of these techniques is to make the margin of error frame by frame substantially higher than a realistic threshold for the auto detection software.
